9: # Crashlytics
10: 
11: This skill provides a complete guide for getting started with Crashlytics on
12: Android or iOS. Crash data collected from client applications can be read using
13: the MCP server in the Firebase CLI.
14: 
15: ## Prerequisites
16: 
17: Provisioning Crashlytics requires both a Firebase project and a Firebase app,
18: either Android or iOS. To read the data collected by Crashlytics, install the
19: MCP server in the Firebase CLI. See the `firebase-basics` skill for references.
20: 
21: ## SDK Setup
22: 
23: To learn how to setup Crashlytics in your application code, choose your
24: platform:
25: 
26: - **Android**: [android_setup.md](references/android_setup.md)
27: - **iOS**: [ios_setup.md](references/ios_setup.md)
28: 
29: ## SDK Usage
30: 
31: The SDK provides a number of features to make crash reports more actionable.
32: 
33: - Add custom keys
34: - Add custom logs
35: - Set user identifiers
36: - Report non-fatal exceptions
37:

40: 
41: - **Android**:

8: ## Project and App Setup

24: ## Add Dependencies to Gradle Build
25: 
26: These changes are made to your Android project's Gradle files.
27: 
28: ### Project-level `build.gradle.kts` (`<project>/build.gradle.kts`)
29: 
30: Add the latest version of the Crashlytics Gradle plugin to the `plugins` block.
31: Fetch the
32: [latest version from the Google Maven repository](https://maven.google.com/web/index.html?q=firebase-crashlytics-gradle#com.google.firebase:firebase-crashlytics-gradle)
33: before adding this.
34: 
35: ```kotlin
36: plugins {
37:     // ... other plugins
38:     id("com.google.firebase.crashlytics") version "<latest_plugin_version>" apply false
39: }
40: ```
41: 
42: ### App-level `build.gradle.kts` (`<project>/<app-module>/build.gradle.kts`)
43: 
44: 1. Add the Crashlytics plugin to the `plugins` block:
45: 
46:    ```kotlin
47:    plugins {
48:        // ... other plugins
49:        id("com.google.firebase.crashlytics")
50:    }
51:    ```
52: 
53: 1. Add the Firebase Crashlytics dependency to the `dependencies` block. It is
54:    recommended to use the Firebase Bill of Materials (BoM) to manage SDK
55:    versions. Fetch the
56:    [latest version from the Google Maven repository](https://maven.google.com/web/index.html?q=firebase-bom#com.google.firebase:firebase-bom)
57:    before adding this.
58: 
59:    ```kotlin
60:    dependencies {
61:        // ... other dependencies
62: 
63:        // Import the Firebase BoM
64:        implementation(platform("com.google.firebase:firebase-bom:<latest_bom_version>"))
65: 
66:        // Add the dependencies for the Crashlytics and Analytics
67:        implementation("com.google.firebase:firebase-crashlytics-ktx")
68:    }
69:    ```

71: ## Follow up Steps
72: 
73: ### Optional: Install the NDK SDK to capture native crashes
74: 
75: If your app uses native code (C/C++), or includes a library with native code,
76: you can configure Crashlytics to report native crashes.
77: 
78: App-level `build.gradle.kts` (`<project>/<app-module>/build.gradle.kts`)
79: 
80: 1. Add the `firebase-crashlytics-ndk` dependency:
81: 
82:    ```kotlin
83:    dependencies {
84:        // ... other dependencies
85:        implementation("com.google.firebase:firebase-crashlytics-ndk:18.6.2")
86:    }
87:    ```
88: 
89: 1. Enable the `nativeSymbolUpload` flag in your `buildTypes` configuration. This
90:    will automatically upload symbol files for your native code, which are
91:    required to symbolicate native crash reports.
92: 
93:    ```kotlin
94:    android {
95:        // ... other config
96:        buildTypes {
97:            getByName("release") {
98:                // ...
99:                firebaseCrashlytics {
100:                    nativeSymbolUploadEnabled = true
101:                }
102:            }
103:        }
104:    }
105:    ```
106: 
107: After these changes, Crashlytics will automatically report crashes in your app's
108: native code.

110: ### Required: Force a Test Crash
111: 
112: To verify that Crashlytics is correctly installed, you need to force a test
113: crash in the app.

120:    import android.os.Looper
121: 
122:    // ... in your Activity's onCreate method or similar startup logic
123:    Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).postDelayed({
124:        throw RuntimeException("Test Crash") // Force a crash after 3 seconds
125:    }, 3000)
126:    ```
127: 
128: 1. Run your app on a device or emulator. The app should crash after a short
129:    delay.
130: 
131: 1. Restart the app. The Crashlytics SDK will send the crash report to Firebase
132:    on the next app launch.
133: 
134: 1. After a few minutes, the crash should be available in the Firebase console.
135:    Go to **DevOps & Engagement** > **Crashlytics** to view your dashboard and
136:    crash reports.
137: 
138: - If the Firebase MCP server is installed, use the `get_report` tool to check
139:   that a crash was received.
140: - As a fallback, visit the Crashlytics dashboard in the Firebase console to see
